results.reasoning: Driven in the built-in browser against a scratch copy served on :4754 (its own home), with app-not-answering's app path set to http://127.0.0.1:4799/x/ and a fixture screen with no design at 127.0.0.1:4799/nodesign/; a python http.server on 4799 was started and stopped as the app. PNGs and probes were re-saved afterwards by a throwaway Playwright script echoing the same states. Every step holds. Opening on the screen, and picking it in the screen picker from the As-built side, both put the design ghost in front at opacity 1 while the app frame holds about:blank, never a refused page. panel.surface-build is disabled with the tooltip 'Nothing answers at 127.0.0.1:4799, so the design is shown. Start the app, or remove this screen's app path.'; panel.app-down reads 'Nothing answers at 127.0.0.1:4799. Start the app, or remove this screen's app path.' as a warning badge (oklch(0.84 0.15 85)) under the bar, pushing the desk down rather than lying over it, matching the accepted design. panel.fade is disabled; clicking App and dragging the fade left it at the design. Starting the server cleared the strip and enabled App within one 3s poll, with a window marker set before the start still present (no reload); choosing App then showed the app's page. The no-design screen shows the strip, an empty frame, and a disabled design side titled 'No design or proposal on file for this screen - a design request is how one gets drawn', which says what the step asks though not in the design's words ('This screen has no design yet. File a design request on it, and a design gets drawn.'). Edges, none failing the rule: put away with the app down, the strip stays at its docked place over the top of the full-bleed design until the panel comes back (estimate 25%, a person putting the panel away to see the design at full size while the app is down; cost a misplaced but still true band); on the no-design screen the App tooltip still says 'so the design is shown' when none is, as the accepted design also does (about 30%, low cost); and leaving the down screen for a screen whose app is on another origin that answers keeps the strip, wrongly telling the person to remove that screen's app path (about 10%, it needs app paths on two origins in one blueprint; the strip stays until the first app answers or the page reloads).
